judged_text: The handler resolves reqBody.userId — the calling instance's user id — directly against the local user table with no cross-instance identity mapping or scoping beyond the shared secret. On any deployment whose local user ids do not mirror the parent's id space, synced credentials are attached to an unrelated local user, so that user's bookings and meetings silently route through a stranger's calendar/video account.

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) trusts `reqBody.userId` from the request body and directly looks up `prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: reqBody.userId } })`, then creates/updates a credential for that `userId` with no cross-instance identity mapping, tenant scoping, or additional validation beyond the shared header secret. If the sending system’s user-id space doesn’t match the receiving Cal.com database (or if the caller supplies an id that exists locally but refers to a different person), the credential will be written to the wrong local user (`prisma.credential.update/create` uses `userId: reqBody.userId`). That matches the finding’s described mis-association risk.
